verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev is built for autonomous background execution. The docs cover cron-scheduled tasks, no execution timeout, automatic retries with exponential backoff, queues and concurrency control, and failure alerts by email, Slack or webhook. An MCP server lets AI assistants trigger, deploy and monitor tasks. Community users independently confirm scheduled and background tasks 'just work' and that it powers an AI automation platform. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of long-running autonomous AI-agent runs (such as chat.agent sessions and waitpoint approvals) beyond vendor docs.
